contract.reader: An engineer or student who has followed entries 1-4, or a practitioner who meets OPC UA, Purdue levels and digital twins in projects and wants precise meanings
contract.problem: How plant control data reach higher-level systems with meaning and status intact, how that link is secured, and what a digital twin is and needs to be useful
contract.outcome: Place functions on ISA-95 levels; explain OPC UA address space, status codes, subscriptions and PubSub versus MQTT; sketch a zones-and-conduits architecture; tell a twin from a shadow, model or visualization; predict and interpret a twin's fault residual and gain trade-off
contract.contribution: A testable definition of a digital twin with the Kritzinger classification and a reproducible leak-detection example with a closed-form residual, set against the protocol and security layers it depends on
contract.evidence: One Python program with real output, re-run over 40 seeds; residual formula derived from the code; IEC 62264-1, IEC 62443, IEC 62541, ISO 23247, ISO/IEC 20922:2016, Kritzinger et al. (2018), Mahnke et al. (2009)
contract.limitations: Architecture level only (no OPC UA programming, no IEC 62443 risk-assessment procedure); linear tank with a fixed-gain observer; the twin cannot distinguish a leak from other unmodeled flows
